note: DTN Content Services cash-bids-table-widget. Read from ONE call to https://api.dtn.com/markets/sites/e0274901/cash-bids?units=us — the site id e0274901 carries this location and its neighbours together, so every one of them is a source file and none of them is new code. IT IS READ THROUGH A BROWSER AND NOT BY A FETCH: DTN answered a server-side probe with "The api key is valid, but it is valid to be used within a browser only", so their gateway scopes these widget keys to browser use. poll.mjs loads https://www.countryvisionscoop.com/grain/cash-bids in a real Chromium and reads the response their own widget asks for, which means we hold no key at all — theirs is public in their page, as it must be for the widget to work. THE LOCATION KEY IS THE NUMERIC location.id (24478) AND NOT THE NAME: a display name is exactly the thing a vendor re-cases, and some of these names are companies rather than towns. cashRounding is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. One run said round-cent (8 testable rows, margin 5) and there is no second run to agree with it. A mode is a property of how they compute their board, so it needs the same answer on a different day's prices. Left off, the identity guard stays exact and a board that does not reconcile refuses loudly instead of publishing under a mode nobody established. COORDINATES ARE NULL AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: the feed carries no coordinate, and a town centroid is a different place from a yard — measured at 1.4 miles on babgrain-auburn. Geocode the street address before relying on a map pin. Built by scripts/dtn-build.mjs from a dtn-probe log; 8 row(s) for this location. STATE AND ADDRESS READ, NOT INFERRED. Premier, Allied, Country Partners, Country Visions and Ag-Land FS each publish their own locations list; the state and street below were read off it on 2026-08-25 and not inferred from the operator's headquarters. TURNED BACK OFF AFTER THE FIRST LIVE RUN, and the reason is written here so nobody re-enables it hopefully. It was refused by the cash - basis = futures identity check. That check is not fussiness: it is what catches a board read half-way through an update, and a wrong cash price is the one thing this whole project refuses to publish. 74 rows: floor explains 30, round 52, ceiling 44. None of the three explains the board. Corn futures trade in quarter cents, so a board displaying cash and basis to the whole cent cannot reconstruct the identity exactly and a residual up to 0.75c is structural rather than a torn read. cashRoundingCents exists for exactly that and would make this pass TODAY -- it is deliberately NOT being used here, because widening the tolerance to three ticks also blinds the torn-read guard for this source, and 'the check went green' is not the same as 'the number is right'. What settles it is one more measurement: capture this operator's raw payload and compare the DISPLAYED cash and basis against the unrounded values in it. Ag-Land and CHS were settled that way in an afternoon -- floor-to-the-cent explained 80 of 80 and 12 of 12, and no tolerance was needed.
publicNote: Their publicly posted cash board, read from the feed their own website reads. Cash and basis are their own commercial numbers. The futures quote is carried only so a consumer can re-check cash minus basis; it is not redistributed as a price feed.
